clue.text: Centre of church inlaid with gold

indicators.note: something inlaid is set into a surface, so the gold goes into the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A gilded inlay sits at the heart of a church's decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: The core of something is its heart or middle part.

clue.text: Miserly person, cold girl collecting loads

indicators.note: to collect is to gather in, so the girl's name with the cold letter wraps around the word for loads

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
Kate is a girl's name
heaps means loads, a great amount

explanation.surface: A chilly young woman gathers up a great pile of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collecting' has the girl wrap around the loads, while the cold letter stays at the front, so the inserted word sits between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A tightwad who hates spending money is a miser.

clue.text: Seeing about

explanation.definitionFit: To regard is to look at, so the participle means looking; as a preposition it means with respect to, a stock synonym of concerning.

clue.text: Bar committee provided with something to write on

parts.note: to black something is to boycott or ban it, as unions black goods
a board is a governing committee

explanation.surface: A pub's management group is handed a notepad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a pub, but here it is a verb meaning to ban: in British union use, workers 'black' goods they refuse to handle.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark classroom panel is written on with chalk.

clue.text: Ball landing on writer's plant

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sitting on another comes above it, so the ball comes first

parts.note: a lob is a ball hit high in tennis or cricket
Elia was the pen name of the essayist Charles Lamb

explanation.surface: A ball comes down onto an author's garden flower.
explanation.walkthrough: ELIA is the pen name of the English essayist Charles Lamb, a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobelias are flowering garden plants, often trailing blue in hanging baskets.

clue.text: See boat caught in reef capsize finally

indicators.note: the caught letter goes inside the word for reef

parts.note: a coral reef, so coral stands for reef
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: takes the last letter of the word capsize

explanation.surface: Look: a vessel trapped on a reef has finally overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' just points the solver at the boat. 'in' puts C inside CORAL, giving CORACL; 'finally' adds E, the last letter of 'capsize'.
explanation.definitionFit: A coracle is a small round Welsh or Irish craft made of wicker covered in hide.

clue.text: Part of sports complex across which a shuttle service operates

definitions.text: Part of sports complex across which a shuttle service operates

parts.words: Part of sports complex across which a shuttle service operates
parts.note: read as transport, a shuttle service runs back and forth; read as sport, the shuttlecock is served over a net on a marked-out playing area

explanation.definitionFit: Shuttlecocks are served across this net-divided playing area in a racket game.

clue.text: Lady wants a good comfortable home mostly

indicators.note: most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a nest is a snug, comfortable home

explanation.surface: A woman wants a pleasant, cosy place to live, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of NEST, leaving NES.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, so a lady could be called this.

clue.text: Loses one's life one day in ancient Rome

definitions.meaning: the Latin word for a day, as the Romans said it

explanation.definitionFit: To perish is to expire, a plain synonym; and in Latin, the language of ancient Rome, the word for a day is spelt the same way.

clue.text: Experts who are strictly for the birds

definitions.text: Experts who are strictly for the birds

parts.words: Experts who are strictly for the birds
parts.note: 'for the birds' is slang for worthless, but taken literally these specialists devote themselves to birds alone

explanation.definitionFit: Scientists who study birds are experts devoted entirely to them.

clue.text: Enthusiastic monarch spanning a number of years

indicators.note: to span is to stretch across, so the monarch's letters surround the period of years

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
an age is a long span of years

explanation.surface: A keen monarch reigns over a long stretch of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen and impatient for something is a plain synonym.

clue.text: Banned car travelling to disco at the farm

indicators.note: letters that travel move about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A forbidden vehicle is driven to a dance held in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustic social dance, traditionally held in a barn, is a country disco.

clue.text: Phenomenon initiated by rough alignment of celestial pair

definitions.text: Phenomenon initiated by rough alignment of celestial pair

indicators.note: the word that starts things off gives only its opening letter
a rough arrangement means the letters are set out in a jumbled order

explanation.surface: Astronomers explain an event brought about when two heavenly bodies nearly line up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initiated' gives P, the first letter of 'Phenomenon'; 'rough alignment of' rearranges CELESTIALPAIR into ARTIALECLIPSE. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: When the Moon only partly covers the Sun, because the bodies are not quite in line, that is this event.

clue.text: So careless breaking dishes

indicators.note: broken pieces are scattered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone so clumsy keeps smashing the crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: Stews cooked slowly in the oven are dishes, named after the pot they come in.

clue.text: His rank must be exceptional as a divine figure

indicators.note: something exceptional is out of the ordinary, so the letters are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: His high status means he must be extraordinary, a godlike person.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu god, the eighth avatar of Vishnu, is a deity.

clue.text: Country school including minimum of science — reverse of very good

indicators.note: the school's name takes in a letter, which goes inside it

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

indicators.note: the least possible part of the word science, its first letter
the letters for very good are read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written here as AI

explanation.surface: A school curriculum with barely any science is the opposite of excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' and 'reverse of' are the indicators. A1 is a British idiom for first-rate, written with the letter I standing for the figure one, so 'very good' gives those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A Baltic republic is a nation state.

clue.text: Terrible Devon side plummeted

indicators.note: something terrible is in a bad way, so the letters are messed up

explanation.surface: A dreadful Devon football team fell sharply down the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible' rearranges DEVONSIDE. Devon is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall steeply and suddenly is a plain synonym, used of planes and prices alike.

clue.text: Label a record made by people in the Philippines

parts.note: a tag is a label
a log is a written record, as in a ship's log

explanation.surface: Islanders produce a tagged recording.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethnic group of Luzon, whose language underlies Filipino, is a Philippine nation.

clue.text: Duck? you could — from duck

definitions.meaning: to lower oneself quickly to avoid a blow
the soft feathers of a duck can be obtained from the bird

explanation.definitionFit: To crouch suddenly is to drop low; and eiderdown, soft feathering, is what you can obtain from a duck.

clue.text: Start book

definitions.meaning: the first book of the Bible

explanation.definitionFit: The word means an origin, and it names the opening book of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Payment that's absurd for one drug

indicators.note: something absurd makes no sense, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A fee for a single dose of medicine is ridiculous.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for a reward or recompense is a payment.

clue.text: Fine expert, judge, may help to determine cause of accident

definitions.text: may help to determine cause of accident

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
a light is a luminary, as in a leading light in a field
a recorder is a part-time judge in English courts

explanation.surface: An excellent specialist magistrate might help investigators work out why a crash happened.
explanation.walkthrough: A recorder in England and Wales is a barrister or solicitor sitting as a part-time judge; 'light' means an expert, as in 'leading light'.
explanation.definitionFit: The so-called black box on an aircraft stores data that investigators study after a crash.

clue.text: Form of insect found in particular valley

indicators.note: the answer is located inside the run of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A particular kind of insect lives in a certain valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A grub or caterpillar is the immature stage of an insect.

clue.text: Longing to have first bit of the problem removed

indicators.note: points at the opening letter of the word for the problem
taken away, so the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: a hitch is a snag or problem

explanation.surface: Someone wishes the opening part of a difficulty would go away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first bit of ... removed' drops H from HITCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A restless craving, as in an urge to travel, is a strong desire.

clue.text: Bride gets carried away and goes over the limit here

definitions.text: Bride gets carried away and goes over the limit here

parts.words: Bride gets carried away and goes over the limit here
parts.note: sounds like a bride overdoing it at the wedding, but by tradition she is carried by the groom over the sill of her new home's doorway; limit also means the doorway itself

explanation.definitionFit: The sill of a doorway is the entrance a bride is traditionally carried across.

clue.text: Have a few drinks etc, and the bar may be spinning round

indicators.note: something spinning turns about, so the word for bar is read backwards

parts.note: a lever is a bar used to prise or lift

explanation.surface: After a few drinks the bar seems to be spinning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub, but it is a metal bar: LEVER, turned round by 'spinning round'.
explanation.definitionFit: To make merry, drinking and partying, is to celebrate noisily.

clue.text: Ah, no singer sadly! And getting worse as such?

indicators.note: something sadly done goes wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lament that a performer is losing their voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges AHNOSINGER. 'as such' refers back to the singer: getting worse as a singer.
explanation.definitionFit: A voice becoming rougher and huskier is deteriorating for a vocalist.

clue.text: Songs of the French — nothing to them!

parts.note: O, the zero shape, means nothing
des is French for of the, plural

explanation.surface: An exclamation that French songs are worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to them' puts O in front of DES.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyric poems meant to be sung are verses, a synonym for songs.
